summary: Toy 11-qubit Hadamard QRW on AWS SV1 demonstrated 18x ballistic-over-diffusive variance growth in 16 Trotter steps. We propose a layered integration where nexus sim-universe consumes a quantum-source random walk as its proposal kernel for trajectory-space exploration.

integration_layers.name: Quantum proposal kernel
integration_layers.spec: Replace classical Metropolis-Hastings random-walk proposal in nexus sim-universe trajectory sampler with a discrete-time QRW step (Hadamard coin + +/-1 lattice shift). For dimension D the cost is D position registers + 1 coin per axis. PoC: D=1, n_pos=10 (1024 sites), T=16 -- this work.

integration_layers.name: QRW-as-oracle endpoint
integration_layers.spec: Expose a nexus tool quantum_walk_step(state, n_steps) that returns a sample from the QRW distribution after n_steps. Backend: SV1 simulator until n <= 30 qubits, then route to IonQ Aria/Harmony QPU once budget is approved. SV1 free-tier (1 hr/month) suffices for ~3000 such calls of the current circuit.

integration_layers.name: Where the quantum advantage applies
integration_layers.spec: Ballistic spreading <x^2> ~ T^2 (vs T classical) means the QRW kernel reaches O(T) lattice distance in T steps -- a quadratic speed-up over classical diffusion-limited exploration. For nexus this matters when (a) the trajectory space has graph diameter > sqrt(burn-in steps available) and (b) the cost of one quantum kernel call is dominated by classical fixed cost. Both are true for sim-universe explorations of conformal-blocks / spin-network state spaces.

integration_layers.name: Honest decoherence budget on real QPUs
integration_layers.spec: On NISQ hardware the ballistic regime survives only while T < T2/(gate_time * gates_per_step). For 10-qubit IonQ Aria (T2 ~ 1s, 2-qubit gate ~ 600us, ~50 gates/step in the QFT-shift implementation) the budget is T_max ~ 30 steps before the QRW collapses to classical diffusion. SV1 (this run) is a noiseless simulator so gives the asymptotic ballistic result.

integration_layers.name: Scaling roadmap (out of scope today)
integration_layers.spec: 1) Push to D=3 lattice (33 qubits) -- still simulable on SV1 within free tier. 2) Move T up to 64 to expose the ballistic regime at >10x ratio. 3) Real QPU validation on IonQ at D=1, T=20 (~$40, requires budget approval). 4) Sim-universe integration via a hexa wrapper that proxies state -> bitstring -> SV1 task -> bitstring -> state. NONE of layers 1-4 are implemented today; only the L0 PoC kernel is empirically validated.

outputs.next_position_int: int sampled from QRW pmf after n_steps
outputs.cost_usd: float (0.0 for sv1 within free tier, ~$0.30/shot for ionq aria)

novelty_disclosure.qrw_theory: Hadamard discrete-time QRW is a well-known result (Aharonov-Davidovich-Zagury 1993; Ambainis-Bach-Nayak-Vishwanath-Watrous 2001). No theoretical novelty in the walk itself.
novelty_disclosure.implementation_novelty: QFT-diagonalized shift using only SV1 native gates (cphaseshift + decomposed-CRZ) is a standard technique; no novelty.
novelty_disclosure.anima_novelty: First end-to-end empirical run of a quantum random walk against a classical baseline as a candidate proposal kernel for nexus sim-universe trajectory sampling. No prior anima track exercised the AWS Braket quantum substrate.
